Proposed for San Diego County

Kids don't just play on this playground.They build it.

Imagine a place where children can pick up a hammer, build a fort, dig a hole, invent a contraption, paint something enormous, or turn a pile of scrap wood into a spaceship.

We're working to bring an authentic Adventure Playground to San Diego County: a community space where kids can build, experiment, collaborate, and discover what they're capable of.

  • No instructions.
  • No predetermined outcomes.
  • No adults telling them what to create.

Currently seeking community partners, potential locations, and supporters.

What is an Adventure Playground?

01

A playground built by kids, not just for kids.

IMGhands.jpg4:5

Close-up: a child's hands hammering a nail into a weathered reclaimed plank, sawdust and bent nails on the board, work gloves nearby. Shallow depth of field, natural light, muted tones.

Adventure Playgrounds are a different kind of play environment. Originating in Denmark in the 1940s and embraced by communities around the world, they put children in charge of their own adventures.

Instead of manufactured playground equipment and carefully prescribed activities, children are given access to open space, reclaimed materials, tools, and the freedom to create.

They might

  1. 01

    Build forts, towers, bridges, and imaginative structures using real wood, hammers, nails, and saws.

  2. 02

    Dig, experiment with water and mud, and explore the natural environment.

  3. 03

    Create art, invent games, and transform everyday materials into something extraordinary.

  4. 04

    Work together to solve problems, negotiate ideas, and tackle challenges.

  5. 05

    Take reasonable risks, make mistakes, and learn through experience.

Supervised by trained playworkers

Trained playworkers supervise the environment, support safe tool use, and step in when necessary, but the children lead the play.

Why San Diego needs this

02

Kids need more opportunities to be kids.

Children today have incredible access to technology, organized activities, and structured learning. But opportunities for independent, imaginative, hands-on play can be harder to find.

We believe there's something important about giving children a space where they can experiment without being told exactly what to do.

  • Where failure is part of the fun.
  • Where a crooked wooden fort is an accomplishment.
  • Where children learn to work together because they have something they want to build.

IMGteamwork.jpg3:2

Three or four kids carrying a long board together across a dirt yard toward a half-built structure. Candid, mid-motion, documentary style. Overcast or soft light, greens and greys.

Outcomes

  • 01

    Creativity & Imagination

    Turning ordinary materials into extraordinary ideas.

  • 02

    Confidence & Independence

    Making decisions, taking initiative, and discovering personal capabilities.

  • 03

    Problem-Solving & Resilience

    Experimenting, making mistakes, and finding solutions.

  • 04

    Collaboration & Community

    Building friendships, sharing resources, and working toward common goals.

  • 05

    Practical Skills

    Learning how to use tools, understand materials, and create things with their own hands.

We want to bring back some of the freedom, creativity, and adventure that made childhood exploration so memorable, while providing a supervised environment designed for today's communities.

Precedent: Sacramento Adventure Playground

03

A decade of imagination, creativity, and community.

We don't have to look far to see what's possible.

In August 2016, Sacramento Adventure Playground opened at the Maple Neighborhood Center in South Sacramento. Operated by Fairytale Town, the program has spent the past decade providing children with opportunities for free, supervised, child-directed play.

Instead of conventional playground equipment, Sacramento provides children with real tools, reclaimed building materials, art supplies, and the freedom to create their own play spaces. Its approach is simple: children learn and grow through experiences they create themselves.

Our goal is to learn from Sacramento's experience and bring a similar opportunity to San Diego County.

Sacramento has shown that this idea isn't just an experiment. It's a model that can serve children and families year after year.

Our vision for San Diego

04

More than a playground. A place that grows with its community.

We envision a permanent, year-round outdoor adventure playground where children have room to build, explore, and create: a space with building materials, tools, open-ended play areas, and structures that evolve over time through the imagination and efforts of the children themselves.

Supported by trained staff who encourage independence while helping children understand tools, materials, and appropriate risks. Welcoming, accessible, and affordable, ideally offering free community play opportunities.

Programs

  1. 01

    Open Adventure Play

    Regular supervised sessions where children direct their own activities.

  2. 02

    Community Play Days

    Opportunities for local families to discover adventure play together.

  3. 03

    School & Youth Partnerships

    Programs connecting children with hands-on, creative experiences.

  4. 04

    Camps & Special Programs

    Optional structured opportunities that help support ongoing operations.

  5. 05

    Community Building

    Volunteer projects, donated materials, and partnerships with local organizations.

Our objective is not to build a high-priced attraction.

It's to create something meaningful for the community that can sustain itself and serve generations of San Diego children.

Let's build something together

05

Seeking land, partnerships, and community support.

San Diego Adventure Playground is currently in the concept and partnership development stage.

We're exploring opportunities to establish a permanent home in San Diego County, particularly through partnerships with organizations that share our interest in children's development, education, recreation, and community life.

Where it fits

  • New Residential Communities

    A distinctive recreational amenity that brings families together, encourages outdoor activity, and creates a lasting neighborhood gathering place.

  • Parks & Community Spaces

    An innovative complement to traditional playgrounds, offering creative, hands-on experiences that conventional recreational facilities rarely provide.

  • Educational & Cultural Organizations

    A natural extension of programs focused on childhood development, creativity, engineering, making, and experiential learning.

  • Businesses & Community Sponsors

    An opportunity to support an accessible, community-focused program through funding, materials, equipment, expertise, or volunteer involvement.

What we're looking for

  1. 01Landowners and developers interested in providing or leasing outdoor space.
  2. 02Community organizations, museums, schools, and recreation providers interested in partnerships.
  3. 03Local businesses willing to contribute building materials, tools, equipment, or financial support.
  4. 04Educators, playworkers, makers, and volunteers who share our enthusiasm for child-directed play.
  5. 05Families and community members who want to help bring this idea to life.

Partnership models

  • Land leases
  • Shared community facilities
  • Sponsorships
  • Collaborative operating arrangements

Our priority is finding the right location and partners to create a safe, sustainable, community-serving playground.
